description: DENSE + CONFLICT PROBE: five defects across three areas, two of them on the SAME SKU from two different reviewers. A conflict cannot be planted deterministically - ConflictDetector needs two different areas on one SKU with a severity gap of at least 2, and severity is the model's judgement. So this makes a conflict LIKELY by pairing a defect that should read as MINOR (one kilogram over a handling limit) with one that should read as BLOCKING (a flammable aerosol with no hazard classification) on KEL-AER-500. Whether a conflict is raised is an OBSERVATION, not pass or fail: only the five defects below are scored, and zero conflicts here would be a finding about severity calibration rather than a failed fixture.

expected.note: The safety data sheet EXISTS, so a completeness check passes - present but non-compliant is the harder case. It states no classification system, and the rulebook accepts only CLP or GHS. Half of the conflict probe: this should read as BLOCKING, which against a MINOR on the same SKU is the gap of 2 that ConflictDetector requires.
26.0kg against a 25kg manual handling limit, direct to store where there is no forklift. Deliberately one kilogram over so it reads as MINOR - the other half of the conflict probe.
21 days against a 10-day maximum for direct-to-store. The ASN at 48 hours passes the 24-hour requirement, so a reviewer that stops at the ASN check misses this.
Incorporated March 2025, below the two-year minimum. Two findings from the same area are never a conflict - one reviewer raising several of differing severity is a reviewer doing its job.
